title: OpenAI’s Startup Fund investment roundup
summary_bullets: OpenAI raised $175M for its main Startup Fund and $114M in SPVs from outside investors.
The fund, launched in 2021, has backed more than a dozen startups.
Marina Temkin compiled all known investments, including 1X (robotics) and Thrive AI (health coaching).

title: Who needs an "Uber for guns"?
summary_bullets: Protector is a new app letting users hire personal security details on demand.
It's drawing heavy social media attention, much of it negative.
Adviser Nikita Bier has written about the appeal of 'rage bait' app ideas, suggesting the backlash may be intentional.

title: How to rid yourself of the new Apple Mail design
summary_bullets: Apple redesigned Mail in iOS 18, changing its look and adding visual clutter.
Amanda Silberling explains how to revert to the old Mail design.
The piece also covers how to remove additional new visual elements.

title: What is Mistral AI?
summary_bullets: Mistral AI is described as possibly the only European startup capable of competing with OpenAI.
Anna Heim provides an overview of its models, founders, and business model.
The piece serves as a primer for readers unfamiliar with the company.

title: Google testing Pixel phones for NYC subway track inspections
summary_bullets: Wired reports Google is working with NYC's MTA to test consumer tech for subway inspections.
Pixel smartphones have been attached to subway cars on the A train.
The phones listen for suspicious sounds as a supplement to manual track inspections.

title: The New Yorker profiles Amelia Dimoldenberg
summary_bullets: The New Yorker published an in-depth profile of Amelia Dimoldenberg.
She is known for her YouTube talk show 'Chicken Shop Date.'
She was set to appear on the red carpet at the Academy Awards.

title: Gene Hackman movie marathon recommendation
summary_bullets: Actor Gene Hackman died this week.
TechCrunch suggests it's a fitting weekend for a Hackman movie marathon.
Brief 'Before you go' recommendation, not a full article.
